title: A year of thinkers

segments.voice: Yesterday, the schools closed, and Marcus Aurelius showed how to leave: one gift, named precisely. Your line was thank you. Did you write your sentence? Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

A bookshelf, four spines. A slim old Chinese book of short chapters. A thick French book of essays that wander. Two Americans who lived in the same small Massachusetts town, one a lecturer, one who went to the woods. This year of the path began with them, long before the science and the schools of practice. Year four is closing now, and the next days look back over it, one part at a time. Today, the four thinkers. The challenge is a hard one: a year of reading, and you get to keep one line from each.
screen: `A BOOKSHELF, FOUR SPINES.` → `YEAR FOUR IS CLOSING.` → `ONE LINE FROM EACH.`

segments.voice: Start with Lao Tzu, and the opening of the Tao Te Ching, in Legge's translation: "The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao." The book begins by admitting that whatever it says will fall short. That's a strange way to open a book, and an honest one. The Way is bigger than any description of it, including this one. Then Montaigne, in France, who turned the honesty on himself. His question, in French: "Que sais-je?" What do I know? Not a sneer at knowledge. A habit of checking. Montaigne wrote about his kidney stones, his cat, his fears, his friend, and he kept asking what he actually knew. Then Emerson, the lecturer, in Self-Reliance: "Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string." After Montaigne's doubt, here is a different note: there is something in you worth listening to. Emerson didn't mean ignore everyone. He meant don't hand your whole inner life to someone else's opinion. And Thoreau, who went to Walden Pond to live deliberately, and came back with two words: "Simplify, simplify." Our life, he said, is frittered away by detail. Set the four side by side and you can hear a kind of conversation. The Way is bigger than words. I may not know as much as I think. Something in me is still worth trusting. And it's easier to hear when life is simpler. Four voices, four lines, one year.
screen: `LAO TZU: THE WAY BEYOND WORDS.` · `MONTAIGNE: WHAT DO I KNOW?` · `EMERSON: TRUST THYSELF.` · `THOREAU: SIMPLIFY, SIMPLIFY.` · then, large: `FOUR VOICES, FOUR LINES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pick one line from each. Settle, and breathe. Bring back each thinker, one per few breaths. Lao Tzu: which line of his stayed with you? It might be the opening, or water, or the valley, or the uncarved wood. Montaigne: his question, or something about friendship, or dancing when you dance. Emerson: trust, or circles, or the over-soul. Thoreau: simplify, or the different drummer, or the morning. Don't search. Let the line that comes first be the one. The bell holds the time.
A year of thinkers. Year four's teachers: Lao Tzu, Montaigne, Emerson and Thoreau, each kept now in a single line. Today's word.
Your line: four lines. Today, write your four down together on one page, a line from each thinker, and read them once more before bed. Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Some readers of Lao Tzu, Montaigne, Emerson and Thoreau keep a commonplace book, copying short lines from each into one notebook and returning to them over time.
